chunks: From him, from Ḥammād, from Shuʿayb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man sleeps and does not perform salat al-maghrib and al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah, or he forgets, then when he awakens before al-fajr with enough time to perform them both, he should perform them both. But if he fears that one of them will escape him, then he should begin with al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah. And if he awakens after al-fajr, then he should begin by performing al-fajr, then al-maghrib, then al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah before sunrise. But if he fears that the sun will rise and one of the two salats will escape him, then he should perform al-maghrib and leave al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah until the sun rises and its rays go away, then let him perform it.

key_terms.تَفُوتَهُ: to pass beyond his ability to perform within its due opportunity
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: sunrise, a limiting time marker in this ruling

ai.seo_question: How should missed maghrib and ʿisha be made up if someone wakes up before or after fajr?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who slept through or forgot salat al-maghrib and al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah when the time of al-fajr has approached or entered. It sets the order of making up the missed salats based on how much time remains before sunrise, showing the legal priority between current and missed obligatory salats.
